INSERT INTO quiz_questions (moduleId, question, options, correctIndex, explanation, sortOrder) VALUES
(60004, 'On a ladder diagram, a normally-open contact is shown as which symbol?', '["Two parallel lines with diagonal slash", "Two parallel vertical lines (no slash)", "A circle", "A zigzag line"]', 1, 'A normally-open contact is two short parallel vertical lines. Normally-closed adds a diagonal slash.', 1),
(60004, 'Cross-reference 5-3, 8-7, 12-1 next to relay CR-10 means what?', '["CR-10 is on pages 5, 8, 12", "CR-10 contacts are on page 5 rung 3, page 8 rung 7, page 12 rung 1", "CR-10 has 3 coils", "CR-10 needs 5V, 8V, or 12V"]', 1, 'Cross-references show where relay contacts are used throughout the drawing set.', 2),
(60004, 'On a P&ID, a dashed line from instrument to process indicates what?', '["Electrical signal", "Pneumatic signal", "Software link", "Capillary tube"]', 1, 'Per ISA-5.1, dashed line = pneumatic signal. Solid = piping, dashed with dots = electrical.', 3),
(60004, 'Wire number 247 most likely belongs to which circuit type?', '["120VAC control", "24VDC control", "Analog signal", "480V power"]', 1, 'Convention: 100-series=120VAC, 200-series=24VDC, 300-series=analog, 400-series=power.', 4),
(60004, 'On a single-line diagram, MCC-1 represents what?', '["A motor", "A Motor Control Center panel", "A single motor controller", "A maintenance computer"]', 1, 'MCC = Motor Control Center containing multiple motor starters and disconnects.', 5),
(60004, 'OL contacts in series with a starter coil represent what?', '["Overload relay contacts that open on excessive current", "Oil level contacts", "Online/offline status", "Operator lockout"]', 0, 'OL contacts open when motor current exceeds the overload setting, dropping out the starter coil.', 6),
(60004, 'What is the purpose of a holding (seal-in) contact?', '["Hold motor at specific speed", "Maintain starter energized after START button is released", "Prevent motor reversing", "Limit starting current"]', 1, 'The seal-in contact keeps the starter energized after the momentary START pushbutton is released.', 7),
(60004, 'Notation 3/14 below a relay coil means what?', '["Rated 3A at 14V", "Located on sheet 3, rung 14", "Has 3 contacts rated 14A", "Installed March 14"]', 1, 'Sheet/rung notation shows the physical location in the drawing set.', 8),
(60004, 'A downward-pointing triangle on a schematic represents what?', '["A fuse", "A ground/chassis connection", "A diode", "A transformer"]', 1, 'Downward triangle is the standard symbol for chassis or earth ground.', 9),
(60004, 'Wire 142 goes to TB-3, terminal 7. How do you find it in the panel?', '["Look for wire 142 anywhere", "Find terminal block TB-3, count to position 7, verify ferrule label 142", "Wire number tells panel location", "Terminal blocks are not labeled"]', 1, 'Find the labeled row, count to the position, verify the wire ferrule matches the drawing.', 10);

INSERT INTO quiz_questions (moduleId, question, options, correctIndex, explanation, sortOrder) VALUES
(60005, 'Per NFPA 79/IEC 60204-1, which stop categories are permitted for E-stops?', '["Category 0 and 1 only", "Category 0, 1, and 2", "Category 0 only", "Any category"]', 0, 'Only Cat 0 and Cat 1 are permitted. Cat 2 maintains power and is NOT allowed for E-stops.', 1),
(60005, 'Minimum safety performance level for E-stop per ISO 13849-1?', '["PLa", "PLc", "PLd", "PLe"]', 2, 'E-stop functions typically require PLd minimum with dual-channel architecture.', 2),
(60005, 'A safety light curtain has 14mm resolution. Minimum detectable object size?', '["7mm", "14mm", "28mm", "Resolution does not determine size"]', 1, 'Resolution equals minimum detectable object. 14mm detects finger-sized objects.', 3),
(60005, 'Purpose of cross-monitoring in dual-channel safety circuits?', '["Double the speed", "Detect if one channel fails differently from the other (discrepancy detection)", "Provide backup power", "Reduce wiring"]', 1, 'Cross-monitoring detects discrepancy between channels, indicating a fault condition.', 4),
(60005, 'In Ds = K x T + C, what does T represent?', '["Temperature", "Total system stopping/response time", "Guard thickness", "Inspection interval"]', 1, 'T = total response time from hazard detection through machine stop.', 5),
(60005, 'What are force-guided contacts in a safety relay?', '["Spring-loaded contacts", "N.O. and N.C. mechanically linked so both cannot be closed simultaneously", "Magnetically held", "Require extra force"]', 1, 'If one contact welds, the linked contact is physically prevented from closing, making faults detectable.', 6),
(60005, 'What must happen before safety system reset after E-stop?', '["Auto-reset when released", "E-stop released AND separate deliberate reset action required", "Machine completes cycle", "Supervisor enters code"]', 1, 'Manual reset is required: releasing E-stop alone must NOT restart the machine.', 7),
(60005, 'Primary purpose of LOTO per OSHA/NFPA 70E?', '["Prevent unauthorized use", "Ensure hazardous energy is isolated and cannot re-energize during maintenance", "Identify ownership", "Schedule maintenance"]', 1, 'LOTO ensures ALL hazardous energy sources are isolated and verified de-energized.', 8),
(60005, 'Why is a coded actuator (tongue-type) switch preferred over a roller-lever?', '["Cheaper", "Cannot be easily defeated with a screwdriver or zip-tie", "Operates faster", "Longer lifespan"]', 1, 'Coded actuators resist defeat because they require the specific matching key shape.', 9),
(60005, 'Difference between safe state and stopped state?', '["Same thing", "Stopped = no motion; safe = all energy controlled so no hazardous release can occur even if a component fails", "Safe is for robots only", "Stopped is more restrictive"]', 1, 'A machine can be stopped but not safe if stored energy could release on component failure.', 10);

INSERT INTO quiz_questions (moduleId, question, options, correctIndex, explanation, sortOrder) VALUES
(60006, 'What does the Integral (I) term in PID eliminate?', '["Oscillation", "Overshoot", "Steady-state error (offset)", "Response time"]', 2, 'Integral accumulates error over time and adjusts output until error reaches zero.', 1),
(60006, 'Loop oscillating. Increasing P gain makes it worse. What to adjust?', '["Increase Integral time (reduce integral action)", "Decrease Derivative", "Increase P further", "Reduce setpoint"]', 0, 'If P worsens oscillation, the loop is too aggressive. Increase Ti to reduce integral contribution.', 2),
(60006, 'Purpose of cascade control?', '["Control two unrelated processes", "Primary controller output becomes secondary setpoint for better disturbance rejection", "Alternate between controllers", "Provide redundancy"]', 1, 'Cascade nests a fast inner loop inside a slower outer loop for improved disturbance rejection.', 3),
(60006, 'In ratio control, what is the wild (lead) flow?', '["The controlled flow", "The uncontrolled flow that varies with process demand", "Maximum flow rate", "Startup flow"]', 1, 'Wild flow varies freely. The controlled (lag) flow is adjusted to maintain the desired ratio.', 4),
(60006, 'Advantage of feedforward over feedback alone?', '["Eliminates sensors", "Corrects for disturbances BEFORE they affect the process variable", "Simpler to implement", "Better steady-state accuracy"]', 1, 'Feedforward acts proactively on measured disturbances before they cause error.', 5),
(60006, 'What is reset windup and how is it prevented?', '["Derivative too large", "Integral accumulates when output saturated - prevented by anti-windup that stops integration at limits", "Proportional band too narrow", "Setpoint changes too fast"]', 1, 'Anti-windup clamps the integral term when controller output is at its limit.', 6),
(60006, 'Fail-closed (air-to-open) valve loses air pressure. What happens?', '["Stays at last position", "Moves to fully closed via spring return", "Moves to fully open", "Oscillates"]', 1, 'Spring drives valve closed when air is lost. Fail position should be safest for the process.', 7),
(60006, 'Ziegler-Nichols ultimate gain method is used for?', '["Sizing valves", "Determining initial PID tuning by finding Ku and Tu at sustained oscillation", "Calibrating transmitters", "Selecting sensors"]', 1, 'Increase P gain until sustained oscillation, then use Ku and Tu in formulas for P, I, D values.', 8),
(60006, 'Split-range: cooling valve 0-50%, heating valve 50-100%. Output at setpoint with no load?', '["0%", "25%", "50%", "100%"]', 2, 'At setpoint with no load, output sits at 50% - the split point where neither valve is open.', 9),
(60006, 'Proportional controller, gain=2, SP=50%, PV=55%, bias=50%. Output?', '["40%", "45%", "50%", "60%"]', 0, 'Output = Bias + Gain*Error = 50% + 2*(50%-55%) = 50% - 10% = 40%.', 10);

INSERT INTO quiz_questions (moduleId, question, options, correctIndex, explanation, sortOrder) VALUES
(60007, '480V/277V wye system: voltage between phase and neutral?', '["480V", "277V", "240V", "120V"]', 1, 'In wye: line-to-neutral = line-to-line / sqrt(3) = 480/1.732 = 277V.', 1),
(60007, 'Purpose of ground fault relay on main switchgear?', '["Protect against overloads", "Detect current to ground indicating insulation failure", "Monitor voltage", "Balance phases"]', 1, 'Ground fault relay detects current imbalance indicating fault current flowing to ground.', 2),
(60007, 'NEC 430.52 maximum breaker size for motor branch circuit (inverse-time)?', '["125% FLA", "175% FLA", "250% FLA", "300% FLA"]', 2, '250% is maximum allowed. 175% is typical starting point.', 3),
(60007, 'What causes single-phasing and why is it dangerous?', '["Voltage surge; causes overspeed", "Loss of one phase; motor draws excessive current on remaining phases causing overheating", "All phases lost simultaneously", "Phase reversal"]', 1, 'Motor runs on two phases drawing ~1.73x normal current, rapidly overheating windings.', 4),
(60007, '75 kVA transformer, 480V primary, 208V/120V secondary. Max secondary FLA?', '["156A", "208A", "361A", "625A"]', 1, 'FLA = kVA*1000/(sqrt3*Vline) = 75000/(1.732*208) = 208A.', 5),
(60007, 'Purpose of selective coordination?', '["All breakers trip together", "Only breaker closest to fault trips, maintaining power to unaffected loads", "Balance load between phases", "Reduce energy costs"]', 1, 'Only the protective device immediately upstream of the fault operates.', 6),
(60007, 'IR scan shows one MCC connection at 185F, adjacent at 95F. What does this indicate?', '["Normal operation", "High-resistance connection generating excessive I-squared-R heat", "Motor overloaded", "Ambient too high"]', 1, '90F rise above adjacent connections = high-resistance joint requiring immediate maintenance.', 7),
(60007, 'Difference between bolted fault and arcing fault?', '["Same thing", "Bolted = near-zero impedance/max current; arcing = arc impedance limits current but generates extreme heat", "Bolted is less dangerous", "Arcing only in DC"]', 1, 'Arcing faults generate 35000F+ plasma - primary cause of arc flash injuries.', 8),
(60007, 'What determines arc flash boundary and PPE level per NFPA 70E?', '["Voltage alone", "Risk assessment: available fault current, clearing time, working distance", "Equipment type", "Worker experience"]', 1, 'Incident energy depends on fault current, clearing time, and working distance.', 9),
(60007, 'Frequent nuisance trips on main breaker during morning startup. Solution?', '["Larger breaker", "Sequenced startup to stagger motor starts and reduce simultaneous inrush", "Larger transformer", "Smaller motors"]', 1, 'Staggered startup spreads inrush demand over time, preventing cumulative trip threshold exceedance.', 10);
